target: Can a non-Sidorenko uniform core acquire a Sidorenko strong expansion? Equivalently, does the expansion converse always hold?
hypotheses: Strong expansion: distinct private degree-one vertices per edge.
Main spectral theorem: bounded symmetric nonnegative r-kernel, constant pair degree p, normalized negative fourth-moment budget B<=r-2.
Dense-host corollary: [0,1]-valued host and constant pair degree; p>=1/[1+(r-2)(r-1)^2].
accepted_conclusions: Global compensated C4/C5 expansion inequality under the spectral budget, including arbitrary-rank L2 and density corollaries.
Sharp binary nonnegative r-lift threshold, with the whole liftable ray and finite tensor products safe.
Tensor closure and normalized-principal-restriction nonclosure of the pair-marginal cone.
Explicit irregular host separates weighted covariance from the regular normalized spectral bound.
Source-scope arguments for Lee nested links and Zhao principal-restriction hypotheses.
remaining_gap: No example of a Sidorenko strong expansion of a non-Sidorenko core and no universal converse. Irregular marginals and all regular marginals beyond the sufficient budget remain unresolved by this work.

supporting_verification_totals.scope: Recorded supporting audit metadata, not proof or new edition-time executions.
